questions.question: Which statement about WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry is correct?
options: WeakRef prevents garbage collection of the referenced object
FinalizationRegistry callbacks are guaranteed to run before the object is collected
Both WeakRef and FinalizationRegistry are primarily used for performance optimization in hot paths
FinalizationRegistry callbacks run asynchronously and have no guaranteed execution timing
questions.explanation: FinalizationRegistry callbacks are scheduled asynchronously by the engine with no timing guarantees and may never run (e.g. process exit). WeakRef allows observation of collection but does not prevent it.

questions.question: What is the output of this code involving iterators and generators?
options: {value: 1, done: false} {value: 2, done: true} {value: undefined, done: true}
{value: 1, done: false} {value: undefined, done: true} {value: undefined, done: true}
{value: 1, done: false} {value: 2, done: false} {value: undefined, done: true}
{value: undefined, done: true} {value: 2, done: true} {value: undefined, done: true}
questions.explanation: The first next() yields 1 (done false). The second next() returns the return value 2 with done true. Subsequent calls return {value: undefined, done: true}.

questions.question: In terms of the JavaScript event loop, which task queue has the highest priority?
options: Macrotask queue (setTimeout, setInterval)
Microtask queue (Promise.then, queueMicrotask)
Animation callbacks (requestAnimationFrame)
Render steps
questions.explanation: Microtasks have higher priority than macrotasks. After each macrotask (or script), the event loop exhausts the entire microtask queue before proceeding to the next macrotask.

questions.question: What is the key behavioral difference when using Proxy with the 'has' trap?
options: The 'has' trap affects the 'in' operator but not Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty
The 'has' trap is only triggered for own properties, not inherited ones
The 'has' trap can prevent prototype chain lookup entirely when it returns false
Using 'delete' on a Proxy always triggers the 'deleteProperty' trap regardless of the 'has' trap
questions.explanation: When the 'has' trap returns false, the 'in' operator returns false immediately without continuing up the prototype chain, effectively hiding inherited properties.

questions.question: Which optimization technique or behavior is true for modern V8 JavaScript engines?
options: Object properties in 'dictionary mode' are faster than hidden classes
Using 'with' statement helps the engine optimize property access
Polymorphic function calls (different hidden classes) are deoptimized to megamorphic state
Inline caches for property access work best with monomorphic call sites
questions.explanation: V8 uses hidden classes (maps) for optimization. Monomorphic (single shape) call sites allow efficient inline caches. Megamorphic state (many shapes) leads to slower generic lookups.

questions.question: What happens when you use a Symbol as a key in a WeakMap?
options: It behaves the same as using a string key
The entry is automatically removed when the Symbol is garbage collected
Symbols are always strongly referenced in WeakMap keys
It throws a TypeError because only objects are allowed as WeakMap keys
questions.explanation: WeakMap keys must be objects (including functions, arrays, etc.). Symbols are primitive values, so using one as a key throws a TypeError.

questions.question: Consider this async generator code. What is the correct way to consume all yielded values?
options: for (const page of fetchPages()) { ... }
for await (const page of fetchPages()) { ... }
fetchPages().then(pages => pages.forEach(...))
fetchPages().next().then(result => ...)
questions.explanation: Async generators must be consumed with 'for await...of' to properly handle the promises returned by each next() call.

questions.question: What is a major downside of using 'new Function()' compared to other dynamic code execution methods?
options: It cannot access variables from the surrounding scope
It bypasses CSP restrictions more easily than eval
It creates a new function with its own lexical scope but shares the global object
It is always faster than eval because of JIT compilation
questions.explanation: Unlike eval(), which runs in the current lexical scope, new Function() creates a function in the global scope only, preventing access to local variables.
